Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 86fbd9f63a6b42b8f158361334f5a25762aea358 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>
Date: Wed, 15 May 2024 10:32:01 -0400
Subject: [PATCH] Bluetooth: hci_sync: Fix not using correct handle

When setting up an advertisement the code shall always attempt to use
the handle set by the instance since it may not be equal to the instance
ID.

Fixes: e77f43d531af ("Bluetooth: hci_core: Fix not handling hdev->le_num_of_adv_sets=1")
Signed-off-by: Luiz Augusto von Dentz <luiz.von.dentz@intel.com>

diff --git a/net/bluetooth/hci_sync.c b/net/bluetooth/hci_sync.c
index 16daa79b7981..a8a7d2b36870 100644
--- a/net/bluetooth/hci_sync.c
+++ b/net/bluetooth/hci_sync.c
@@ -1194,7 +1194,7 @@ int hci_setup_ext_adv_instance_sync(struct hci_dev *hdev, u8 instance)
 
 	cp.own_addr_type = own_addr_type;
 	cp.channel_map = hdev->le_adv_channel_map;
-	cp.handle = instance;
+	cp.handle = adv ? adv->handle : instance;
 
 	if (flags & MGMT_ADV_FLAG_SEC_2M) {
 		cp.primary_phy = HCI_ADV_PHY_1M;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/bluetooth/hci_sync.c`**
- The line that sets the `cp.handle` has been modified. 
- Previously, it was set directly to the `instance` variable: `cp.handle = instance;`
- It has been changed to conditionally set the handle based on the existence of an advertisement instance: `cp.handle = adv ? adv->handle : instance;`

### Relationships Between Modifications
- The modification addresses a bug related to the advertisement handle being incorrectly set. By changing the assignment of `cp.handle`, the code now ensures that it uses the correct handle from the advertisement instance (`adv->handle`) if it exists, rather than defaulting to the instance ID. This change is crucial for scenarios where the advertisement handle may differ from the instance ID, thereby improving the functionality of the advertisement setup process.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
cp.handle = instance;
```
Reason:
The code incorrectly assigns the advertisement handle using the instance ID directly, which may not correspond to the correct handle associated with the advertisement instance. This can lead to improper management of advertisement instances, especially when multiple advertisement sets are present.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
cp.handle = adv ? adv->handle : instance;
```
Reason:
The fix changes the assignment to use the handle associated with the advertisement instance (`adv->handle`) if the advertisement instance exists. This ensures that the correct handle is used during the advertisement setup, preventing issues related to incorrect handle usage when managing multiple advertisement instances.
